Last September, after Apple unveiled the iPhone 17, the countdown began on whether the new flagship could break a record set 15 years ago. That record is more than a year from being broken, but based on current rumours, the iPhone 17 will be the first model to challenge it.

The iPhone 4 had an unusually long run on sale

The record is held by the iPhone 4, which went on sale in June 2010 and remained Apple's top-tier iPhone until October 2011. Because Apple shifted its flagship launch cycle from summer to autumn that year, the iPhone 4 held top dog status for nearly 16 months.

For customers planning to 'wait for the iPhone 5,' that period was particularly frustrating. What Apple ultimately released was the iPhone 4S, which looked almost identical to the iPhone 4. All the improvements were internal: Siri made its debut, the camera was upgraded, and performance was boosted.

The iPhone 4 technically had several launch moments. AT&T was then iPhone's exclusive carrier partner in the US, and it launched first. Six months later, Verizon became the second US carrier partner. After that, following 10 months of delays, a long-awaited white version finally arrived.

Since then, no iPhone has matched the iPhone 4's longest record of 15 months as the flagship. The closest was the iPhone 11 Pro, which held a 13-month lead because pandemic-related delays pushed back the iPhone 12. Other exceptions exist—for instance, the gaps between the iPhone SE and the SE 2, and on to the iPhone 16e, each stretching more than four years—but those were intentional, not flagship cycles.

The iPhone 17 will break the record (but with a difference)

The iPhone 18 is expected to arrive only in spring 2027. That means the iPhone 17 will hold the top spot in Apple's main lineup for roughly 18 months, surpassing the iPhone 4's record and setting a new benchmark for the longest run as the standard iPhone.

Model Launch Replaced by Duration at top iPhone 17 September 2025 iPhone 18, Spring 2027 (expected) ~550 days, ~18 months (projected) iPhone 4 iPhone 4S 477 days, ~15.7 months iPhone 11 Pro iPhone 12 Pro 399 days, ~13.1 months iPhone (2007) iPhone 3G 378 days, ~12.4 months

A key difference between the iPhone 4 era and today is the existence of the Pro line. The gap from the iPhone 4 to the 4S was an upgrade drought for customers waiting for something new.

I suppose it depends on how you define 'flagship'

During this cycle from the iPhone 17 to the iPhone 18, the Pro models will still arrive on schedule each year, alongside what is expected to be Apple's first foldable iPhone.

The foldable iPhone will be the biggest hardware change in iPhone history, but the iPhone 17 is still expected to take the record for the longest gap between standard flagship models.

The shortest iPhone cycle

Incidentally, the record for the shortest gap between two iPhone generations may surprise you. The cycle from the iPhone 12 to the iPhone 13 is memorable, because Apple adjusted its pace after pandemic-related delays, making that cycle last only 11 months.

Yet although the iPhone X was announced in September 2017, because it did not actually go on sale until November 2017, it was replaced by the iPhone XS after just 10 months.
